purpose: Reconcile the workbook's participant sheets against the article's reported n, so a partition rule can be stated without inferring the analysis population from sheet order.

identifiableEventRule.definition: count of distinct integer BroadSceneNum values on a participant's sheet
identifiableEventRule.articleExclusion: participants with fewer than two identifiable events recalled were dropped from transition analyses

reconciliation.note: Conditions map to the article's four experiments in order. Conditions 3 and 4 reconcile exactly on both enrolled and analysed counts; conditions 1 and 2 each carry one sheet more than the article's enrolled n.

byCondition.experiment: original nonlinear film, free recall any order
byCondition.agreement: analysed matches; enrolled differs by one

byCondition.experiment: original nonlinear film, recall in presented order
original nonlinear film, recall in chronological order
restitched linear chronological cut, free recall any order

partitionRule.statement: Use only sheets present in the subs index (130), then drop sheets with fewer than two distinct BroadSceneNum values, yielding 123 participants at 27/33/30/33.
partitionRule.residual: One participant more than the article analyses, located in condition 2. Record this rather than silently matching the article's count; the surplus sheet is not identifiable from the workbook alone.
doNotDo: infer the population from sheet order
use the three sheets absent from the subs index
treat condition as an instruction tweak rather than a separate experiment

keyContrast.statement: Condition 1 versus condition 4 holds film content, runtime and free-recall instruction fixed while varying only whether presentation order carries the chronology.
keyContrast.use: the within-dataset probe of whether a monotone prior tracks presentation order or story order
keyContrast.supportingArms: conditions 2 and 3 vary recall instruction with the nonlinear stimulus held fixed

nonClaims: the surplus condition-2 participant has been identified
the condition-to-experiment mapping is stated in the release
identifiable-event counts reproduce the article's own exclusion arithmetic
membershipMethod: Pinned workbook subs index intersected with sheets; >=2 distinct integer BroadSceneNum values, independent of accuracy eligibility
